Hi Camila,

We're working through the SIG questionnaire ahead of our security review next week. A few of our reviewers need clear mappings for the three hosting modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private/VPC/on-prem): specifically, which controls/dataflows apply to each, and what artefacts we can expect to receive.

Top asks:
- Short bullets that map each mode to SIG sections (data residency, network control, logging, key management, support model).
- Canonical evidence files we can attach to our SIG submission (architecture diagram, sample logs, SOC 2 summary).
- Any customer action required for Private (VPC peering, firewall rules, KMS integration steps).

Can you send a concise packet we can include in our SIG response? Our timeline is tight — would appreciate a reply by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Anna Liao
Security Lead, Marigold Systems

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a compact, auditor-friendly mapping you can paste into the SIG workbook; I also attached the artefacts we typically include. If you want, we can convert this into a one-page PDF for submission.

Quick mapping (Hosted | Dedicated | Private (VPC/on-prem))

1) Data residency & isolation
- Hosted: Multi-tenant control plane; customer data isolation via logical separation and per-tenant encryption. We provide region selection for data processing and storage. Evidence: redwood_deployment_modes_v1.pdf (page 3), soc2-summary-2025.pdf (controls on encryption at rest).
- Dedicated: Dedicated GPU pools and tenant VLANs — stronger throughput isolation and dedicated storage buckets. Evidence: network_diagram + tenancy notes in deployment packet.
- Private: Customer-managed VPC or on-prem appliance; customer controls network egress/ingress. Evidence: redwood_network_diagram.png, sample VPC checklist (attached).

2) Network control & ingress rules
- Hosted: TLS termination at edge; strict ACLs between services. Customers do not manage inbound networking.
- Dedicated: Option for customer-managed peering; we support IP allowlists and private connectivity.
- Private: Full customer control — VPC peering, ExpressRoute/Direct Connect, or air-gapped on-prem. Include firewall rule templates and recommended NACLs.

3) Key management & encryption
- Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS with per-tenant keys; customer-managed keys (BYOK) available for enterprise tier.
- Dedicated: BYOK strongly recommended; we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed key wrapping.
- Private: Customer KMS/HSM is the norm — we provide integration steps and example IAM policy. Evidence: soc2-summary-2025.pdf, sample-access-logs.txt (shows encrypted object metadata).

4) Logging, auditing & retention
- Hosted: Centralized logs retained per your plan; audit logs available via Console and export.
- Dedicated: Longer retention options; tenant-level access logs and performance traces.
- Private: Logs remain in customer-managed storage unless agreed otherwise. Evidence: sample-access-logs.txt, Console dashboard links.

5) Support & SLAs
- Hosted: Standard support + best-effort SLAs for free tiers; SLA-backed uptime for paid hosted customers.
- Dedicated: SLA-backed throughput + prioritized support.
- Private: Enterprise support contracts with on-call escalation and runbook sharing.

Attachments included (zip of evidence in this thread):
- redwood_deployment_modes_v1.pdf (mapping + short architecture)
- redwood_network_diagram.png
- soc2-summary-2025.pdf (high-level SOC 2 report summary)
- sample-access-logs.txt (redacted log sample for auditors)

If you want a short paragraph per SIG question instead of bullets, say the word and we'll reformat. Happy to hop on a 20-min call with your reviewer Wednesday morning.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Anna — quick follow-up with the minor clarifications Ben requested. I've attached a one-page PDF you can include in the SIG workbook (redwood_deployment_modes_v1.pdf includes the fallback note on page 2). A couple of points to help your reviewer: 

- Dedicated fallback: By default we will route to an equivalent hosted model variant when Dedicated capacity is exhausted. Customers on strict isolation plans can opt to fail closed instead — we document this as a rollout policy setting and will list it in the SIG notes.
- Audit logs ownership: For Private deployments audit logs remain under customer control. For Hosted/Dedicated they are managed by Redwood; retention is configurable via the Console and we can export copies on request.

Next steps:
1) I attached the short packet (same files as before).
2) If Marigold wants a limited NDA'd transfer of the full SOC 2 report, we can route that through legal — please let me know the reviewer email and I'll open the request.
3) Happy to schedule a 20-min sync with your security reviewer Weds 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
